items.text: Wash hands and don PPE if appropriate
Introduce yourself including your name and role
Confirm the patient's identity
Explain the examination and gain consent
Position the patient appropriately (sitting at 45 degrees)
Ensure adequate exposure of the chest while maintaining dignity
Inspect the patient from the end of the bed for respiratory distress, cachexia, or accessory muscle use
Assess oxygen delivery devices and sputum pots
Observe respiratory rate and pattern
Inspect hands for clubbing, peripheral cyanosis, tar staining, or asterixis
Check pulse rate and rhythm
Measure capillary refill time if indicated
Inspect eyes for anaemia or cyanosis
Inspect mouth and tongue
Assess jugular venous pressure if relevant
Palpate cervical and supraclavicular lymph nodes
Inspect the anterior chest for scars, deformity, asymmetry, or visible pulsations
Palpate for chest expansion and tactile vocal fremitus
Percuss the anterior chest systematically
Auscultate the anterior chest systematically comparing sides
Ask the patient to sit forward and inspect the posterior chest
Palpate posterior chest expansion and tactile vocal fremitus
Percuss the posterior chest systematically
Auscultate the posterior chest systematically comparing sides
Assess vocal resonance or whispered pectoriloquy if performed
Check peak flow or spirometry if relevant to the case
Thank the patient and restore clothing
Summarise examination findings to the examiner or patient
